method: Read published figures and archive images in a background browser. No source images were copied into the repository or added to the Folio capture catalog.
scopePolicy: Only visible static frames or plates were inspected. Product/version, source-publication and screenshot-creation dates remain separate. No usability, responsive execution, motion or whole-site quality verdict follows from these checks.

checks.subject: Apple web homepage, 2001 record
checks.distinction: Clean organization coexists with depth; the page is not wholly flat.

checks.subject: ViewPoint successor figure in the 1989 Star retrospective
checks.distinction: A later successor figure supports lineage; it is not a launch-day 1981 Star screenshot.

checks.subject: Museum of Dirt, 1996 record
checks.distinction: Grunge details do not imply maximal density or disorder in every region.

checks.subject: 2Advanced v1, 2000 record
checks.distinction: Flash is the medium; the shown technical vocabulary is the visual evidence. Motion was not tested.

checks.subject: eBoy, 1999 record
checks.distinction: A coherent pixel world exceeds a single pixel icon; game behavior is not established.

checks.subject: Platinum Appearance control-panel figure
checks.distinction: Native appearance has specific system context; generic gray styling alone is insufficient.

checks.subject: XP login illustration published in the 2025 retrospective
checks.distinction: A later-published historical illustration is not proof of its original screenshot date.

checks.subject: Windows 7 pre-release illustration
checks.distinction: The frame identifies a testing build; it is not Vista launch output or the first appearance of Aero.

checks.subject: Mac System 1.1 rendered in an archive screenshot
observations: Menus, compact controls and overlapping windows
checks.distinction: The on-screen clock reflects later screenshot creation, not the software's original release.

checks.subject: Workbench 1.0 rendered in an archive screenshot
checks.distinction: This is a named platform reference, not a label for every blue/orange pixel design.

checks.subject: Windows 95 rendered in an archive screenshot
checks.distinction: Directional bevels and strong control roles differ from low-relief same-material neumorphism.

checks.subject: BeOS R5.0.1 PE rendered in an archive screenshot
checks.distinction: The R5 example does not establish the first BeOS tab's date.

checks.subject: Neumorphic versus Material card diagram
observations: Same-base low relief on one card
Visually separate elevated surface on the other
checks.distinction: This explains surface relationships; it is not a functional app or production-adoption measurement.

checks.subject: Official expressive phone UI plate
checks.distinction: Only the visible portion was reviewed. No animation, unseen screen or complete task flow inherits a claim.

checks.subject: Glass concept-card illustration
observations: Translucent upper card over colored forms
checks.distinction: The named concept illustration does not verify real banking software or date its graphic creation.

checks.subject: Clay-like dashboard montage
checks.distinction: This is conceptual UI imagery; functioning dashboard behavior and production adoption were not established.

checks.subject: Google search homepage, 1998 record
observations: Sparse content with supporting link groups
checks.distinction: Minimal composition is not synonymous with every element being flat. The example is not minimalism's origin.

checks.subject: New York Times web page, 1996 record
observations: Section navigation integrated with reading order
checks.distinction: The newspaper aesthetic has visual evidence beyond the subject being news. Its content date is not necessarily screenshot creation.
